title: Mental Performance Consultants’ Experiences Consulting With High-Performance Coaches
abstract: The broad aim of this study was to understand mental performance consultants’ experiences of consulting directly with coaches. Twelve mental performance consultants (female n = 5; age range = 27–75) who had consulted with high-performance coaches on aspects of their own performance participated in one approximately 60-min semistructured interview and follow-up member checking. Using thematic analysis, we produced 16 themes related to research questions on relationship development (themes: coach beliefs, relationship building, benefiting athletes first); performance needs (themes: communication and feedback, mental skill development, work–life balance, facilitating connection, leadership dynamics); barriers (themes: lack of buy-in and trust, lack of time, organizational limitations); ethical considerations (themes: confidentiality, peer supervision, relationship boundaries); and training preparation (themes: formal and informal education). This research provides insight into how mental performance consultants navigate consulting with high-performance coaches and discusses training needs for such consulting work.
